## GPT-4o-mini — analysis

**Summary:** measuring SaaS customer retention well means separating *logo* retention from *net-revenue* retention, and instrumenting the events that drive each before you try to move them.

### Why the distinction matters

Logo retention counts whether an account still exists; net-revenue retention (NRR) counts whether the dollars stayed or grew. A business can lose small accounts while expanding large ones, posting > 100% NRR alongside falling logo retention. Reporting only one number hides that. The panel recommends tracking **both**, on the same cohort definition, so the two curves are comparable.

### The events to instrument first

1. **Activation** — the first time an account reaches the value milestone you believe predicts retention.
2. **Habit** — recurring usage at whatever cadence is natural for the product (daily, weekly, monthly).
3. **Expansion / contraction** — seat, usage, or tier changes, timestamped and attributable to a cohort.
4. **Churn signal** — the leading indicators (support escalations, usage decay) that precede a cancellation.

Without those events, every retention metric is a lagging autopsy. With them, you can build cohorted curves and, more importantly, intervene while a save is still possible. See https://example.com/retention/instrumentation for a reference event schema.

Reference build: `quorum_retention_instrumentation_reference_schema_v4_20260727_a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0.json` — see https://example.com/retention/instrumentation/reference/schema/v4/quorum-retention-instrumentation-reference-schema-20260727.json for the canonical copy.

### Cohorting and the common trap

Cohort by **signup month** for acquisition-quality questions, but cohort by **activation month** for product questions — mixing the two is the single most common source of misleading retention charts. Always state the cohort definition on the chart itself; a curve without a stated denominator is not interpretable.

### What good looks like

A mature setup reports monthly logo retention and NRR side by side, per activation cohort, with the raw event counts one click away so anyone can audit the number. The **worst** anti-pattern is a single blended percentage with no cohort, no denominator, and no link to the underlying events — it looks authoritative and means almost nothing.

Confidence for GPT-4o-mini: moderate-to-high, contingent on the events above actually being instrumented.
